(a) Inventory Sales Preferences.—Section 335(c) of the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act (7 U.S.C. 1985(c)) is amended—
        (1) in paragraph (1)—
            (A) in subparagraph (B)—
                (i) in the subparagraph heading, by inserting “; socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “or rancher”; 
                (ii) in clause (i), by inserting “ or a socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “or rancher”; 
                (iii) in clause (ii), by inserting “or socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “or rancher”; 
                (iv) in clause (iii), by inserting “or a socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “or rancher”; and 
                (v) in clause (iv), by striking “and ranchers” and inserting “or ranchers and socially disadvantaged farmers or ranchers”; and  
            (B) in subparagraph (C), by inserting “or a socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “or rancher”;  
        (2) in paragraph (5)(B)—
            (A) in clause (i)—
                (i) in the clause heading, by inserting “; socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “or rancher”; 
                (ii) by inserting “or a socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “a beginning farmer or rancher”; and 
                (iii) by inserting “or the socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “the beginning farmer or rancher”; and  
            (B) in clause (ii)—
                (i) in the matter preceding subclause (I), by inserting “or a socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “or rancher”; and 
                (ii) in subclause (II), by inserting “or the socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “or rancher”; and   
        (3) in paragraph (6)—
            (A) in subparagraph (A), by inserting “or a socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher” after “or rancher”; and 
            (B) in subparagraph (C)—
                (i) in clause (i)(I), by striking “and ranchers” and inserting “or ranchers and socially disadvantaged farmers or ranchers”; and 
                (ii) in clause (ii), by inserting “or socially disadvantaged farmers or ranchers” after “or ranchers”.    
    (b) Loan Fund Set-Asides.—Section 346(b)(2) of such Act (7 U.S.C. 1994(b)(2)) is amended—
        (1) in subparagraph (A)—
            (A) in clause (i)—
                (i) in subclause (I), by striking “70 percent” and inserting “an amount that is not less than 75 percent of the total amount”; and 
                (ii) in subclause (II)—
                    (I) in the subclause heading, by inserting “; joint financing arrangements” after “payment loans”; 
                    (II) by striking “60 percent” and inserting “an amount not less than ⅔ of the amount”; and 
                    (III) by inserting “and joint financing arrangements under section 307(a)(3)(D)” after “section 310E”; and   
            (B) in clause (ii)(III), by striking “2003 through 2007, 35 percent” and inserting “2008 through 2012, an amount that is not less than 50 percent of the total amount”; and  
        (2) in subparagraph (B)(i), by striking “25 percent” and inserting “an amount that is not less than 40 percent of the total amount”.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments that extend inventory sales preferences to socially disadvantaged farmers or ranchers and adjust loan fund set-aside percentages. The tempting reading is that naming farmers and ranchers, who are outside parties, signals participation, but they appear only as beneficiaries of loan and sales preferences, not as parties consulted on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking authority, or right to sue.
fable.s: (b) Loan Fund Set-Asides.—Section 346(b)(2) of such Act (7 U.S.C. 1994(b)(2)) is amended—

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to existing statutes regarding eligibility preferences for inventory sales and loan fund set-asides for specific groups of farmers. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. The changes are substantive policy adjustments rather than procedural participation mechanisms.
qwen_block.s: Section 335(c) of the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act (7 U.S.C. 1985(c)) is amended

opus.w: The section only makes wording changes that extend inventory sales preferences to socially disadvantaged farmers or ranchers, and it adjusts the percentages of loan funds set aside. Outside parties appear only as people who may receive benefits (buying property or getting loans). Applying for benefits is excluded by the definition and is not consultation on a federal decision. There is no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation requirement, or right to sue.
opus.b:
**Step 1 – Analysis.** One could misread this section as participation because it adds "socially disadvantaged farmers or ranchers," who are outside the government. But that doesn't work under the definition. The section only gives these farmers preferences in inventory sales and changes the percentages of loan funds set aside. Buying farm inventory or getting a loan is a benefit or application, not a role in a federal decision. The section has no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue.

**Step 2 – Label.**

qwen_chat.w: The text only amends eligibility criteria for loans and inventory sales preferences. It does not require the government to consult with these groups or allow them to participate in the decision-making process; it simply defines who can apply for benefits. Applying for benefits is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.

qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "socially disadvantaged farmer or rancher" and "beginning farmer or rancher," which are outside parties.
Resolution: The text only amends eligibility criteria for loans and inventory sales preferences. It does not require the government to consult with these groups or allow them to participate in the decision-making process; it simply defines who can apply for benefits. Applying for benefits is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
